topic: Kubernetes labels and selectors — patterns and commands
linkedin_hook: Mastering Kubernetes labels and selectors is a game-changer for efficient cluster management, and I'm sharing my top commands and patterns to get you started!
linkedin_intro: As a senior DevOps engineer, I've worked with numerous Kubernetes clusters and seen firsthand the impact of well-organized labels and selectors. In this cheatsheet, I'll share the most useful commands and patterns I've learned over the years. From basic syntax to advanced techniques, this guide covers everything you need to know to take your Kubernetes skills to the next level.

pro_tips: Use the --dry-run flag to test label updates before applying them to your cluster, for example: kubectl label --dry-run --overwrite pod <pod-name> <label-key>=<label-value>
Utilize the --record flag to keep track of changes made to your resources, for example: kubectl label --record pod <pod-name> <label-key>=<label-value>
Leverage set-based label selectors to simplify complex queries, for example: kubectl get pods -l 'set in (dev, prod)'
Take advantage of the -o jsonpath flag to extract specific information from your resources, for example: kubectl get pods -l <label-key>=<label-value> -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'
